entries.sense_en: in a safe place where nothing can hurt you

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word for the state; the idiom stresses keeping away from a nearby danger.
synonyms.example: The children are safe at home.

synonyms.nuance: Means not blocking or not bothering others, with no idea of danger.
synonyms.example: Move your bike out of the way.

synonyms.nuance: Hidden or sheltered, especially from rain or from being seen.
synonyms.example: We waited under cover until the storm passed.

entries.sense_en: a whale, dolphin or porpoise; a scientific name, used here as a grand, flattering title
entries.sense_ko: 고래류(고래·돌고래 등을 이르는 학술어) — 여기선 고래를 치켜세우는 거창한 호칭

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; ‘cetacean’ sounds scientific, which is why the flattering fish uses it.
synonyms.example: We saw a whale from the boat.

synonyms.nuance: Wider group that also includes seals and sea otters, not only whales and dolphins.

entries.sense_en: full of small hard lumps, so not smooth to eat

synonyms.nuance: Common word for food or surfaces with lumps, often a complaint (lumpy gravy).
Usually about roads, rides or surfaces you move over, not food.
Has hard rounded bumps, often bones or wood (knobbly knees); a little humorous.

entries.sense_en: to go somewhere, get something, and bring it back

synonyms.nuance: Only the carrying toward the speaker; ‘fetch’ includes going there first.
Most common and informal; can mean fetch, buy or receive.
synonyms.example: Can you get the milk from the fridge?

synonyms.nuance: Formal; getting back something lost, left or stored.
synonyms.example: She retrieved her bag from the lost-and-found.

entries.sense_en: to become covered with a mass of small white bubbles

synonyms.nuance: Very close; ‘foam’ is more neutral, ‘froth’ suggests light, messy bubbles on a liquid’s surface.
synonyms.example: The waves foamed on the rocks.

synonyms.nuance: Bubbles rising with a hissing sound, as in soda.
synonyms.example: The cola fizzed in the glass.

synonyms.nuance: Water moving violently round and round, not the bubbles themselves.

entries.sense_en: trousers (an old-fashioned word)

synonyms.nuance: Standard British word for the same garment.
American everyday word; in British English it means underwear.
synonyms.example: He spilled coffee on his pants.

synonyms.nuance: Trousers that end above the knee.

entries.sense_en: two straps over the shoulders that hold trousers up

synonyms.nuance: The British word for the same thing; British ‘suspenders’ hold up stockings.
synonyms.example: He wore red braces with his suit.

synonyms.nuance: Goes around the waist instead of over the shoulders.

entries.tip_ko: 미국식 ‘멜빵’. 영국에서 suspenders는 스타킹을 고정하는 끈이라 혼동 주의.

entries.sense_en: a large knife whose blade folds into the handle

synonyms.nuance: Smaller and lighter folding knife, often with one short blade.
synonyms.example: He sharpened the pencil with a penknife.

synonyms.nuance: General word for any folding knife carried in a pocket.

entries.sense_en: a sailor

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; ‘mariner’ is literary or old-fashioned.
Official or naval word, also a rank.
Formal, stresses a life spent travelling by sea.

entries.sense_en: the ability to understand things well and make wise decisions

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; often from age and experience rather than sharp thinking.
Practical cleverness, especially in business or judging people; can be slightly calculating.
Quick intelligence; can be showy and not always wise.
synonyms.example: She solved it with great cleverness.

entries.tip_ko: ‘infinite-resource-and-sagacity’는 ‘무궁무진한 재치와 지혜’를 한 덩어리 별명처럼 붙여 쓴 말장난입니다.

entries.sense_en: completely alone, with nobody else around

synonyms.nuance: Plain fact of being by yourself; not used before a noun.
Adds sadness about being alone; ‘solitary’ is neutral.
synonyms.example: She felt lonely in the big city.

synonyms.nuance: Only one of its kind in that place; used only before a noun.
synonyms.example: a lone tree on the hill

entries.sense_en: to let something hang or drag loosely behind or in the water

synonyms.nuance: Pulling something heavy along with effort; ‘trail’ is loose and relaxed.
synonyms.example: He dragged the box across the floor.

synonyms.nuance: Hanging freely and swinging in the air, not through water or along the ground.
synonyms.example: Her legs dangled over the edge.

synonyms.nuance: Putting something into liquid briefly and taking it out.
synonyms.example: Dip your toes in the pool.

entries.sense_en: permission to do something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; ‘leave’ in this sense is old-fashioned or formal.
Formal agreement, often legal or medical.
Approval plus warm support, especially from family.
synonyms.example: They married with her father’s blessing.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 ‘떠나다’가 아니라 명사 ‘허락’. ‘휴가(annual leave)’도 원래 ‘자리를 비워도 된다는 허락’에서 나온 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: to walk or play with bare feet in shallow water

synonyms.nuance: Walking through water, often deeper and with effort; not playful.
Making water fly up noisily; focuses on the noise and spray.
Moving through water without touching the bottom.

entries.tip_ko: ‘노를 젓다’ 뜻도 있지만, 영국 영어에선 아이들이 얕은 물에서 노는 것을 주로 paddle이라 합니다.

entries.sense_en: to open and close your lips noisily to show you enjoyed food

synonyms.nuance: Usually before eating, showing you want something; ‘smack’ is often after.
synonyms.example: He licked his lips at the sight of the cake.

synonyms.nuance: Enjoying taste slowly and quietly, with no noise.

entries.sense_en: to move around quietly, like an animal hunting

synonyms.nuance: Wandering freely over a wide area with no aim, not secretly.
Moving secretly to avoid being seen, not necessarily hunting.
synonyms.example: He sneaked out of the house.

synonyms.nuance: Following one particular target closely and secretly.

entries.sense_en: to cry or shout very loudly

synonyms.nuance: Long, high, sad cry of grief or pain.
synonyms.example: The mother wailed for her lost child.

synonyms.nuance: Crying with short noisy breaths; about sadness, not loudness.
Loud shout, often in anger or excitement, without tears.

entries.sense_en: a lively dance done alone, traditionally by sailors

synonyms.nuance: Fast, bouncy folk dance, especially Irish; not linked to sailors.
synonyms.example: They danced a jig at the wedding.

synonyms.nuance: Quick Scottish or Irish dance for couples or groups.

entries.sense_en: to make short sudden sounds in the throat you cannot control

synonyms.nuance: Same word, modern spelling; far more common today.
Letting air up from the stomach through the mouth, not a throat spasm.

entries.sense_en: no (an old word)

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word.
Very casual spoken form of ‘no’.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날엔 투표의 ‘반대’(yeas and nays)나 장난스러운 말투에서만 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: quite the opposite; very different from that

synonyms.nuance: Modern standard way to reject what was said and state the opposite.
synonyms.example: “Are you tired?” “On the contrary, I feel great.”

synonyms.nuance: Everyday spoken phrase with the same meaning.

entries.sense_en: connected with the place or time of your birth

synonyms.nuance: Common word for where you were born (native land, native language).
Everyday and warm; the place you belong to now, not only birth.

entries.sense_en: should, because something bad will happen if you don’t

synonyms.nuance: General advice; ‘had better’ is stronger and hints at a bad result.
Like ‘should’, a little more about duty; less urgent than ‘had better’.
synonyms.example: You ought to call your mother.

synonyms.nuance: Strong necessity or rule, not just a warning.

entries.tip_ko: ‘~하는 편이 낫다’보다 경고 느낌이 강해서, 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있습니다.

entries.sense_en: a frame of crossed bars that lets water or air through but blocks larger things

synonyms.nuance: Decorative bars over a window, door or car front.
Any pattern of crossing lines, including on paper or maps.
Criss-cross strips of wood or metal, often decorative, in a fence or window.

entries.tip_ko: 형용사 grating은 ‘귀에 거슬리는’(a grating voice)이란 전혀 다른 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: in a pattern of lines that cross each other many times

synonyms.nuance: Across or diagonally, one crossing only rather than a repeated pattern.
Sharp turns one way then the other along a single line; lines don’t cross.
synonyms.example: The path zigzagged up the hill.

entries.sense_en: very, completely (informal, before an adjective)

synonyms.nuance: Neutral intensifier; ‘good and’ is folksy and suggests thoroughly done.
Formal; stresses that something was done completely.
Same pattern but pleasant, approving tone (nice and warm).
synonyms.example: The soup is nice and hot.

entries.tip_ko: ‘좋고 단단한’이 아니라 ‘아주 단단히’. good은 뜻 없이 강조만 합니다.

entries.sense_en: to say a poem or text aloud from memory

synonyms.nuance: Saying words from a page, not from memory.
Repeating words rhythmically, often in a group or singing tone.
Formal; speaking dramatically, like an actor or orator.
synonyms.example: He declaimed the speech to the hall.

entries.sense_en: to tell a story or report what was said

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; ‘relate’ in this sense is formal and literary.
Telling events in order, often from personal experience.
synonyms.example: He recounted his adventures at sea.

synonyms.nuance: Telling a story as a storyteller or voice in a film.
synonyms.example: The film is narrated by an old man.

entries.tip_ko: ‘관련시키다/공감하다’로 흔히 알지만 여기선 ‘이야기해 주다’입니다. ‘proceed to relate’ = ‘이제 들려주겠다’.

entries.sense_en: a mass of small smooth stones on a beach

synonyms.nuance: The individual small stones; ‘shingle’ is the whole stony beach surface.
synonyms.example: She collected pebbles by the sea.

synonyms.nuance: Small rough stones used on paths and roads, not rounded by the sea.
Tiny grains, much finer than shingle.
synonyms.example: The sand was hot under our feet.

entries.tip_ko: 미국에선 주로 ‘지붕널’ 뜻으로 알려져 있어요. 이 해변 뜻은 영국 영어에서 흔합니다.

entries.sense_en: the strip of wood or stone at the bottom of a doorway

synonyms.nuance: Same thing, more common and also used figuratively (on the threshold of change).
synonyms.example: He carried her over the threshold.

synonyms.nuance: The step just outside a door, not the strip inside the frame.
synonyms.example: The parcel was left on the doorstep.

synonyms.nuance: The same kind of ledge but at the bottom of a window.
